comparator.name: Health and Society
comparator.sourceNotes: Current BGM 2026 handbook:132 compulsory taught credits +18 compulsory thesis +30 open choice=180; no formal track selected. Two additional zero-credit safety obligations. Complete all132 taught credits, including all60 first-year credits, before the thesis in this coherent example; this exceeds the current102-prescribed-credit threshold and includes YRM21806 Data Analysis and HSO31306 Literature Reviews. YSS84818 requires the named Health and Society thesis guide; its publicly indexed same-code guide has2023 logistical dates, not asserted a new2026 publication. Its102/allB1/data-analysis entry rules are satisfied by the completed prescribed course set; current2026 programme/module rules control. No specific chair-topic or obsolete dated timetable is imposed. Current module content and programme sequencing resolve the pathway without an invented new source gate.

components.name: Introduction to Health and Society
components.note: The programme approaches health through society, behaviour, prevention and health systems. General safety is an additional zero-credit requirement.

components.name: Research Methods in the Social Sciences
Global Challenges and Communication in a Changing World
Introduction to Epidemiology and Public Health
Environmental Assets for Health
components.note: Includes field research on environmental determinants and healthy neighbourhood design. Complete the additional zero-credit fieldwork safety requirement before field activities.

components.name: Preventing Disease and Improving Population Health: an Interdisciplinary Approach
Health Demography and Global Population Transitions
components.note: Population-health research uses quantitative methods alongside the concurrently taught Data Analysis course.

components.name: Data Analysis for Health and Society
Literature Reviews for Health and Society
components.note: Required third-year preparation in systematic and scoping literature reviews and critical appraisal.

components.name: BSc Thesis Health and Society
components.note: Required 18-credit independent research project, combining a literature review with empirical research, a report and oral presentation and defence. Complete at least 102 prescribed credits, including all first-year credits, before starting. This example completes the prescribed taught courses first, including Data Analysis and Literature Reviews.

components.name: Minor and/or free-choice electives
components.note: Thirty credits of minor and/or elective study complete the bachelor. The choice remains open; examples of possible minors are not compulsory routes.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest response sustains population health, social/behavioural determinants, policy and evidence. The inequality/institutions programme then prioritises legal, redistributive and collective governance questions; the behaviour/communication programme changes the priority to behavioural evidence and audience-directed interventions. Pairwise differences are6/7/12courses (45/52.5/90EC), with9/9/7advanced courses and current feasible schedules. All twelve generator interests have exact ownership. The alternative healthy-environment theme is already addressed by the closest and policy programmes; no unrelated fourth programme is manufactured.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both teach disease measures, epidemiological study designs, bias and public-health evidence. The programmes differ in applications and scope.
Both directly teach social influence, attitudes, group behaviour and the social-psychological study of behaviour.
Both directly study health behaviour, stress and coping, mental health and biopsychosocial evidence. UCR also emphasises patients and medical settings; WUR includes a quantitative group study.

The UCR programme combines public health and social sciences across several courses. No single selected course integrates the WUR introduction’s health systems, history, prevention and societal determinants.
No selected course provides the full global-health and health-promotion framework, international priority setting and health-system collaboration.
Social and health psychology contribute to behaviour, but no selected course sustains the specific biological, psychological and socioeconomic study of nutrition behaviour.
Climate and governance courses support environmental-health interests but do not reproduce the integrated neighbourhood health field-research and healthy-design assignment.
Public health, health psychology and communication contribute to prevention, but no single separately placed course integrates the WUR multilevel infectious/chronic disease-prevention framework.
Lifespan psychology studies individual development; it does not supply population demographic measures, transitions and quantitative health-demography research.

Public goods, equity, redistribution, health expenditure and social insurance directly address public allocation for a healthy society. WUR additionally teaches dedicated health-economic evaluation and wider economic perspectives.
Organisational culture, collaboration, leadership and change address an important organisational part of healthcare innovation. WUR’s patient-centred and frugal innovation design is not reproduced.

Misinformation, scientific trust, cognitive/social vulnerabilities and health/climate communication address an important part of the WUR course. WUR additionally teaches agenda setting, media and political communication across countries.

Ethical theory and critical moral argument supply a central part of reasoning about health, justice and autonomy. WUR concentrates on health-policy dilemmas; UCR has broader philosophical applications.

Policy-making phases, national/international arenas, a sugar-policy case and policy memos directly address policy analysis. WUR focuses more fully on health systems, participatory health promotion and policy networks.
Both teach sociological theory, social structure and inequality. WUR applies these throughout to health; UCR develops broader social cases.
Speech preparation and delivery, persuasive appeals and feedback-based communication practice address the specific presentation-skills function. UCR is a larger rhetoric course.

Theory-based persuasive messages, implementation with community partners and reflective evaluation address the communication part of behaviour-change intervention. WUR additionally requires systematic health Intervention Mapping and broader determinant/implementation planning.
No selected course provides the dedicated historical study of demographic, epidemiological, nutritional and welfare-state transitions.
No selected course sustains the specific sociological study of eating customs, food identity, access and health across cultural settings.
Both develop research questions and social-science research design, including experimental and nonexperimental approaches. The UCR course adds statistical analysis and an empirical project.

Regression, group comparisons, categorical outcomes and R-based research analysis share substantial quantitative methods. WUR also integrates qualitative analysis, mixed methods and survival analysis.
Both teach systematic literature searching, selection and critical evidence appraisal. UCR additionally develops quantitative meta-analysis; WUR also teaches scoping reviews.

Foundational statistical content occurs within broader selected methods courses, which are placed against their strongest research-design and data-analysis relationships; no separate course is duplicated here.
Inference and regression occur in the selected methods sequence. Those courses are placed against research design and data analysis rather than duplicated as a separate statistics course.
The required 18-credit WUR thesis differs from scheduled UCR courses. Optional UCR independent research is shown separately, outside each 180-credit programme.
This is genuine open elective space, without an invented course counterpart.

notes.text: Wageningen offers a dedicated social-scientific health curriculum with nutrition behaviour, population demography, healthy-environment fieldwork, health intervention design and a required 18-credit thesis. audience.programmeDescription: Health and Society studies how behaviour, social conditions, environments and public decisions shape health. Psychology, sociology, economics and research methods support prevention, healthier communities and health policy.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The three UCR programmes approach these interests through population health and social policy, inequality and public institutions, or behavioural evidence and public communication. Dedicated nutrition, health demography, healthy-neighbourhood fieldwork, systematic health-intervention design and the required thesis remain important differences.
